title: Magnetic properties of rare earth clusters
claim: Among clusters that remain superparamagnetic at all studied temperatures, Tb17 has an internal moment per atom that is independent of temperature, whereas Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, Dy27, and Gd22 have internal moments per atom that increase with vibrational temperature.
explanation: Internal moments are obtained by substituting the measured effective moment into the Langevin function. For these clusters the extracted moment is constant versus field at fixed temperature. Tb17 is 3.49 ± 0.21 μB per atom at all temperatures and fields, similar to transition-metal clusters, while Table 1 shows the other listed clusters rising with temperature. The authors suggest intracluster antiferromagnetic coupling as a possible extra mechanism.
scope: Gd22, Tb17, Tb22, Tb27, Dy22, and Dy27 in the superparamagnetic regime.
conditions: Vibrational temperatures about 73-303 K; low-field Langevin approximation μ_eff ≈ N μ^2 B / 3kT when NμB/kT ≪ 1, with the full Langevin form used for the reported internal moments.
caveats: The antiferromagnetic interpretation is proposed, not demonstrated. Some Table 1 entries are missing or have large uncertainties, especially Dy at high temperature.
